content.comment_body: Hello everyone. I searched through the [product_name] software but couldn’t find a timer that starts on a falling edge and activates an output. Is there a way to achieve this? Any advice is appreciated.

If the trigger event for the timer happens, you can initiate a switch-off delay using a rising edge. Once the delay ends, use a latching relay activated by a falling edge to control the output. The latching relay will then switch the output. You didn’t specify when or how the output should turn off. A suggested solution has been attached.

Thanks for your response. In my process, I need the timer to begin only after the input drops to zero (the falling edge). From there, it should count for 2 seconds, enable a digital output, and ideally auto reset, preferably using a single button or input. Is this setup possible?
You can use a retentive on-delay. See the attachment for details.
Perfect. This is exactly what I needed. Thanks so much for everyone's help.

analysis.insight_summary: The user struggled to locate a timer function in the [product_name] configuration software that can be triggered by a falling edge. The lack of an obvious solution created uncertainty about whether such a function was supported. With input from other community members, the user discovered that a retentive on-delay can be used, demonstrating that flexible timer setups are possible even though they may not be immediately apparent.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is looking for a simple and easily available function or timer block that operates on a falling edge, and can also automate subsequent actions—ideally integrated into a straightforward and intuitive workflow within the software.
